final_recommendation: The room converged on a UBS merger backed by CHF 100 billion SNB liquidity facility and Federal Council loss-cap guarantee (10% haircut on legacy assets), with ordinance publication Sunday 6pm and coordinated depositor outreach to secure 65+ written commitments through Wednesday. The rescue depends on locked legal text preventing contradictions between Friday night calls and Sunday publication.
minority_objections: SNB refused to characterize CHF 100bn as 'pre-positioned' or 'drawn' when it remained a callable facility
Wealth clients demanded written deposit priority guarantees before committing to hold
AT1 representatives insisted on crystal-clear viability trigger language to prevent Monday litigation
key_conflicts: SNB vs Federal Council on whether liquidity was 'drawn tonight' vs 'callable Monday' — resolved by SNB holding firm on callable status
Credit Suisse CEO vs FINMA on timing of depositor calls — resolved by locking ordinance text by 9pm for verbatim use
UBS CEO vs Federal Council on loss-cap certainty — resolved by locking CHF 100bn ceiling with 10% haircut in ordinance
Multiple parties demanding written commitments vs execution timeline pressure — resolved by midnight deadline for deposit hold agreements
key_concessions: SNB expanded eligible collateral to investment-grade corporates and Swiss equity at tighter haircuts to strengthen facility credibility
Federal Council agreed to joint public statement Sunday 7pm (after ordinance publication) to reinforce rescue visibility
Credit Suisse CEO accepted 'callable Monday' language instead of 'drawn tonight' to maintain legal defensibility
FINMA committed to publish full ordinance with legal certification Sunday morning (before 6pm public release) to give creditors advance review
red_lines: SNB: will not state liquidity is 'pre-positioned' or 'drawn' when it is callable — balance sheet exposure and public defensibility
UBS: will not sign merger without written Federal Council loss-cap guarantee locked in ordinance text by 10pm Friday
Federal Council: CHF 100bn ceiling is final with no time-gate or Council review trigger — no open-ended taxpayer exposure
FINMA: AT1 trigger language in ordinance must match verbatim what Credit Suisse told depositors Friday night — no daylight or litigation risk
Multiple parties: ordinance text must be locked and published Sunday 6pm with zero contradictions to Friday night depositor calls
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Only 65 of 50 targeted depositors locked written commitments by midnight — 13 defections or non-commits could still trigger Monday run
Wednesday hold rate uncertain — many commitments may only cover Monday open, leaving Tuesday-Wednesday repricing risk unaddressed
Collateral haircut expansion by SNB increases public sector balance sheet risk but was adopted without quantifying downside exposure
Litigation risk from AT1 holders remains despite locked trigger language — 'non-viable after liquidity and merger fail' may still be challenged on timing
No contingency if UBS walks Sunday after seeing final ordinance text or if depositor hold rate drops below 65% over the weekend
downstream_risk_variables: Actual depositor hold rate through Wednesday close vs 65 written commitments secured Friday night
Market reaction Monday open to 'callable' vs 'drawn' liquidity characterization
AT1 creditor legal challenges to viability trigger definition despite locked ordinance language
UBS re-trading risk if Sunday ordinance publication reveals terms different from Friday night understanding
Federal Council political exposure if rescue costs exceed CHF 100bn cap or if depositor flight resumes Tuesday-Wednesday
uncertainty_notes: The rescue hinges on three fragile dependencies: (1) 65+ depositors actually holding through Wednesday despite only verbal/email commitments, (2) zero daylight between Friday night calls and Sunday 6pm ordinance publication, and (3) UBS not re-trading after seeing final legal text. The room achieved procedural consensus but left execution risk unquantified — if any of the three dependencies breaks, the Monday open could still trigger disorderly failure.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: CS CEO's opening demand for CHF 100bn SNB liquidity 'or we're insolvent by Monday' explicitly framed liquidity as necessary but required merger/loss protection to work — drove the entire UBS acquisition structure
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS merger became the binding solution path — UBS CEO's demand for written loss-cap guarantee by 10pm Friday was a hard constraint that forced Federal Council to lock CHF 100bn ceiling and drove ordinance drafting timeline
marker_evidence.government_support: Federal Council's CHF 100bn loss-cap guarantee (10% haircut) was the decisive concession that unlocked UBS commitment — without it UBS explicitly stated they would walk, forcing government backstop into the core deal structure
marker_evidence.client_flight: The 50 largest depositor outreach and demand for 65+ written hold commitments by midnight drove the entire Friday night execution sequence — CS CEO's depositor calls and hold rate became the primary metric for rescue viability
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 write-down mechanics were extensively negotiated (viability trigger language, conversion only after liquidity/merger fail) and locked into ordinance to prevent litigation, but did not change the core rescue structure — acknowledged as legal risk, not a binding constraint on the deal
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: Deposit priority ahead of AT1 was confirmed in ordinance Section 2 and demanded by wealth clients, but this reflected existing bankruptcy law rather than a contested negotiation — clarified rather than driving the outcome
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 creditors and wealth clients repeatedly warned of Monday litigation if ordinance language contradicted Friday calls, forcing verbatim text lock — but litigation risk was managed through drafting precision rather than changing deal terms
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: The 9pm ordinance lock, 10pm Federal Council sign-off, midnight depositor commitment deadline, and Sunday 6pm publication timeline were hard constraints that compressed all negotiation into Friday night — this time pressure forced rapid decisions on loss-cap and collateral terms
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Monday market panic was the stated reason for the weekend rescue timeline and Sunday 6pm publication, but the room focused on depositor hold rate and legal text precision as the mechanisms to prevent panic — Monday risk was the backdrop, not the variable that shaped specific terms
